explorerTopology.title: High-Write GPS Ingestion & Atomic Driver Dispatch
explorerTopology.subtitle: Regional H3 spatial grid + Redis lock to guarantee single-rider matching
explorerTopology.overview: Updating a disk SQL database 500,000 times/sec for moving drivers would destroy B-Tree indexes. Instead, Location Service updates an in-memory city-sharded H3/Geohash index (only 128 MB RAM globally!) and emits a Kafka trail for offline analytics, while Dispatch uses atomic locks (`SET NX EX`) so a driver only sees one ride offer at a time.
keyTakeaways: Keep active moving driver locations in RAM (H3 / Geohash) with short TTLs; flush raw GPS breadcrumbs asynchronously via Kafka to cold/TSDB storage.
Hexagonal H3 cells eliminate corner-distance distortion vs square grids and support instant `kRing(1)` neighbor lookup.
Region-shard by `city_id` so Mumbai traffic never shares database or lock contention with London.

chaosScenarios.title: Two Riders Compete for Last Driver + Offer Timeout
chaosScenarios.triggerSummary: Rider A and Rider B both query the same sparse H3 cell with only Driver d_901 nearby; d_901 then ignores Rider A's offer.
chaosScenarios.mitigationSummary: Rider A wins atomic `SET NX` lock (Rider B skips to next candidate); after 15s timeout or decline, lock deletes and Dispatch expands search to `kRing(2)`.

steps.info: Rider A acquires lock:driver:d_901; Rider B receives NIL -> immediately skips to candidate #2
steps.payloadInspector: SET lock:driver:d_901 trip_B NX EX 15 -> (nil) -> zero double-booking
steps.inspectorNote: Fails fast in <1ms rather than blocking on a slow SQL row lock.

steps.info: Driver d_901 declined -> lock released -> Dispatch widens radius to kRing(2) (19 H3 cells)
steps.payloadInspector: Expanding spatial search ring from 0.7km to ~2.1km radius
steps.inspectorNote: Hierarchical H3 grids make radius expansion deterministic without expensive trigonometric full-table scans.

deepDives.title: Why H3 Beats Quadtree for Moving Drivers
deepDives.bottleneck: Re-splitting and merging dynamic Quadtree nodes under 500k coordinate mutations/sec causes heavy lock contention.
deepDives.solution: Fixed-resolution H3 cells act as O(1) hash buckets—moving a driver is just `SREM old_cell` + `SADD new_cell`.
deepDives.tradeoff: Downtown cells hold more drivers than rural cells, handled by sub-filtering top N or choosing resolution 8/9.

deepDives.title: Road-Network ETA vs Straight-Line Distance
deepDives.bottleneck: A driver 300m away across a river or highway divider might take 14 minutes to reach pickup.
deepDives.solution: Use H3 spatial search to shortlist top-20 nearby candidates cheaply, then call a Routing/ETA Graph Engine (OSRM / contraction hierarchies) only on those 20.
deepDives.tradeoff: Two-stage funnel avoids running expensive graph shortest-path across thousands of drivers.

criteria: Recognizes active spatial state fits in RAM
Contrasts H3/Geohash vs Quadtree for moving objects
Queries neighbor rings to avoid boundary misses
Prevents double-dispatch with atomic driver locks + TTL
Keeps trip transitions ACID in regional SQL
Distinguishes H3 straight-line recall vs road-network ETA
